info.title: Cafe Ops
info.description:
Read-only back-office API for Sasha's Corner.

**Every route is a GET except two**: `POST /api/templates/{id}/preview`, which writes
nothing, and `POST /api/templates/{id}/apply`, the composition editor's commit. There is
no route that creates, confirms or sends a purchase order -- invariant 1 says that needs
a human in Telegram.

**Encoding.** Money is integer pence where the database stores an integer, and an exact
decimal *string* of pence where the figure is derived and fractional. Quantities are
always strings. A missing cost is `null`, never `0`. A low-confidence forecast has
`qty: null` and its reasons populated -- render the reasons *in place of* the number,
because the number is not in the payload. See `GET /api/meta`.

**Auth.** One shared password (spec 1: no user management). Send it as `X-API-Key` or
`Authorization: Bearer`. With `CAFEOPS_API_PASSWORD` unset every route but
`/api/health` answers 503.

ApplyResponse.title: ApplyResponse
ApplyResponse.description:
The edit, applied from today. The old component row is closed, a new one opened.

There is no retroactive mode (invariant 3). `effective_from` before the start of
the local trading day is refused with 409.

effective_expiry.title: Effective Expiry
effective_expiry.description: Earlier of the carton date and opened_at + open_life_days.

days_left.title: Days Left
days_left.description: Null when this ingredient does not expire.

ChannelDayOut.title: ChannelDayOut
ChannelDayOut.description:
One reported day. The series the aggregates above are computed from.

Exposed because an aggregate answers "how much" and hides "was it steady".
A null field means that day did not report it -- it is NOT a zero, and a
sparkline must break rather than dip to the floor.

ChannelFinding.title: ChannelFinding
ChannelFinding.description: Ranks well, converts badly: the cheapest thing on the channel screen to fix.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Provenance of the rows. A hand export and a scrape are not equally trustworthy.

net_pence.title: Net Pence
net_pence.description: Contribution after commission AND ad spend, over the days that reported all three. A day missing one is dropped whole rather than part-subtracted.

daily.title: Daily
daily.description: The reported days in order, so a trend is visible rather than only a total. Covers only the days that reported -- 9 of a 28-day window today.

ingredient_name.title: Ingredient Name
ingredient_name.description: Null when the slot is filled by a variant axis.

ingredient_cost.description: Cost per unit of the slot's ingredient, if it has one.

ComponentOut.title: ComponentOut
ComponentOut.description: One template slot. `qty_by_size` is strings in and strings out (ARCHITECTURE 7.4).

qty_by_size.title: Qty By Size
qty_by_size.description: Per-size quantities as decimal strings, e.g. {"S": "0.12", "M": "0.18"}.

window_days.title: Window Days
window_days.description: Sales window for the COGS projection.

actor.title: Actor
actor.description: Who is applying this. Recorded on the cost rollup's trigger.

qty_by_size.title: Qty By Size
qty_by_size.description: Per-size quantities as decimal strings, e.g. {"S": "0.12", "M": "0.18"}.

window_days.title: Window Days
window_days.description: Sales window for the COGS projection.

ComponentQtyChange.title: ComponentQtyChange
ComponentQtyChange.description:
The body of both `/preview` and `/apply`.

Quantities are **strings**. A float here is refused by the service layer
(`edit_composition._validated`) and by this schema's type, in that order.

pence.title: Pence
pence.description: Exact decimal pence as a string, or null when the cost is unknown.

source.title: Source
source.description: Weakest PriceSource among the ingredients behind this figure (INVOICE|ESTIMATE|SUPPLIER_FEED), or null when the cost is unknown.

is_estimate.title: Is Estimate
is_estimate.description: True when any ingredient behind this figure is priced ESTIMATE.

is_missing.title: Is Missing
is_missing.description: True when at least one ingredient behind it has no price.

excluded_from_aggregates.title: Excluded From Aggregates
excluded_from_aggregates.description: True when this figure was left out of the totals on the same response, so the reader is told rather than left to infer it from a total that does not add up.

Cost.title: Cost
Cost.description:
A money figure and how much it is worth trusting. Invariant 8.

`pence` is an exact decimal string of pence, or `null` when unknown. It is never
`0` for "unknown": zero is a real and different claim.

emergency_total_premium_pence.title: Emergency Total Premium Pence
emergency_total_premium_pence.description: Null rather than a partial sum when any line cannot price its own premium. A total missing two of five lines understates the argument it exists to make.

emergency_notes.title: Emergency Notes
emergency_notes.description: Cases deliberately NOT routed to retail. The half that stops this becoming a licence to shop.

DriftAttributionOut.title: DriftAttributionOut
DriftAttributionOut.description:
Which problem this is, and therefore what to fix. Spec 5.2's v2 diagnostic.

The two fixes are opposite -- order less versus change the recipe -- so a single
undifferentiated percentage sends the reader the wrong way about half the time.

DriftOut.title: DriftOut
DriftOut.description: The latest observation, the gate's verdict, and the attribution behind both.

premium_pence.title: Premium Pence
premium_pence.description: Extra actually paid by going to retail. Never negative. Null when unpriced.

raw_premium_pence.title: Raw Premium Pence
raw_premium_pence.description: Signed. Negative means retail was cheaper for this line.

retail_is_cheaper.title: Retail Is Cheaper
retail_is_cheaper.description: A sourcing finding, not a premium: the preferred supplier is the wrong default for this ingredient. Surfaced separately so it is arguable rather than absorbed into a zero.

EmergencyLineOut.title: EmergencyLineOut
EmergencyLineOut.description:
A Tesco run: what could not wait, and the retail premium it cost. Spec 4.4.

Two premium figures, and the difference is load-bearing. `premium_pence` is the extra
actually paid and is never negative. `raw_premium_pence` is signed, and when it is
negative `retail_is_cheaper` is true: retail would have been cheaper for this line all
along, which is a **sourcing finding** about the wrong default supplier, not a saving
to net off the cost of panic-buying. A screen that showed only the signed figure could
make a week of emergencies look like a discount.

qty.title: Qty
qty.description: Total forecast quantity over the window, or null when low-confidence.

Forecast.title: Forecast
Forecast.description:
A forecast, or the reason there is no number to show. Invariant 9.

When `is_low_confidence` is true, `qty` is `null` and `reasons` carries the
sentence to render **in its place**. The figure is withheld from the payload
deliberately; see the module docstring.

Health.title: Health
Health.description: Open, unauthenticated. Says whether the door is locked, never what the key is.

cost_delta_pence_per_item.title: Cost Delta Pence Per Item
cost_delta_pence_per_item.description: One figure only when every affected item agrees. Null when they do not -- an average across items that disagree is a number describing nothing.

cost_delta_pence_range.title: Cost Delta Pence Range
cost_delta_pence_range.description: The spread, when `cost_delta_pence_per_item` is null. `ImpactPreview` itself puts this only in a warning sentence; it is computed here from the per-item deltas so a screen can render a range rather than parse prose. See the integrator note about `ImpactPreview`.

true_margin_delta_pence_per_item.title: True Margin Delta Pence Per Item

rank_moves.title: Rank Moves
rank_moves.description: (item label, margin-per-minute rank before, rank after) for items the edit moves.

LabourImpactOut.title: LabourImpactOut
LabourImpactOut.description:
Spec 5.6's half of the preview.

`labour_cost_pence_per_item` is one figure only when every affected item agrees;
otherwise it is null and `labour_cost_pence_range` carries the spread. An average
across items that disagree is a number describing nothing.

orderings_agree.title: Orderings Agree
orderings_agree.description: Expected false. True on a real menu means every ranked item takes the same time to make, or the prep times are not real.

excluded.title: Excluded
excluded.description: (label, reason) for items that cannot be ranked. Named, never sorted to the bottom as zeroes.

allow_conflicts.title: Allow Conflicts
allow_conflicts.description: Accept the LOWEST quantity at each size where the legacy rows disagree, and record that the choice was made. Arbitrary by construction -- the resulting quantities need verifying against the real recipes.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: The whole result as one sentence, written by the backend.

Meta.title: Meta
Meta.description: Conventions and vocabularies, so the frontend does not hard-code enum strings.

basis_label.title: Basis Label
basis_label.description: Human label for the basis: 'counted + ledger' or 'ledger only - NO COUNT'.

is_negative.title: Is Negative
is_negative.description: The ledger has consumed more than the last count recorded. Count it.

OnHand.title: OnHand
OnHand.description:
A stock figure that cannot be serialised without saying what kind it is.

Invariant 6. `is_theoretical` is always true -- this is the ledger's number, not a
count. `has_count_basis` is the one that matters operationally: false means the
figure is a bare movement sum with no physical anchor behind it, which is not good
enough to order against.

forecast.description: Over the EFFECTIVE cover window -- the one the line was sized on, which a shelf-life or season cap may have shortened.

cover_days.title: Cover Days
cover_days.description: The effective cover window this line was sized on.

full_cover_days.title: Full Cover Days
full_cover_days.description: The uncapped window: lead time + gap to the next delivery + safety days.

forecast_full_window_qty.title: Forecast Full Window Qty
forecast_full_window_qty.description: Forecast over the FULL window. Null when the forecast is withheld (invariant 9) -- the difference of two withheld numbers is still the number.

capped_out_qty.title: Capped Out Qty
capped_out_qty.description: Quantity deliberately NOT ordered because of the cap. The answer to 'by how much?', as a number rather than only inside cap_detail's prose.

cap_reason.title: Cap Reason
cap_reason.description: Invariant 4. Set when shelf life or a season shortened this line's cover window, e.g. 'capped at 5 days -- Whole milk shelf life'. The user must see that the system under-ordered ON PURPOSE, or they will override it and create the waste the cap prevented.

cap_detail.title: Cap Detail
cap_detail.description: The arithmetic behind the cap: by how much, and from what.

is_top_up.title: Is Top Up
is_top_up.description: Added to clear a minimum or free-delivery threshold. Never a perishable (invariant 5).

clamped.title: Clamped
clamped.description: 'min_qty' or 'max_qty' when a par clamp moved the number.

PreviewResponse.title: PreviewResponse
PreviewResponse.description: What the edit WOULD do. This endpoint writes nothing -- see `views.preview_edit`.

ingredient_name.title: Ingredient Name
ingredient_name.description: Null when the slot is filled by a variant axis rather than a fixed ingredient.

qty_by_size.title: Qty By Size
qty_by_size.description: Size code -> quantity as an exact decimal STRING. Never a float.

quantities.title: Quantities
quantities.description: Menu item name -> the quantity it uses.

describe.title: Describe
describe.description: The conflict as one sentence, written by the backend.

ProposalConflictOut.title: ProposalConflictOut
ProposalConflictOut.description: Legacy rows that disagree about one quantity. A human decides which is right.

proposal_id.title: Proposal Id
proposal_id.description: The stable, unambiguous handle. NAMES ARE NOT UNIQUE -- detection names a group after its defining ingredient, so two different recipes can share one. Always confirm by this.

is_hollow.title: Is Hollow
is_hollow.description: No components and no axes: there is no recipe here. Confirming is refused, because it would create an empty template and strip its items of the manual recipes they resolve through today.

name_is_ambiguous.title: Name Is Ambiguous
name_is_ambiguous.description: Another proposal shares this name. They are different recipes.

already_materialised.title: Already Materialised
already_materialised.description: A real template of this name already exists; confirming again is refused.

blocked_reason.title: Blocked Reason
blocked_reason.description: Why this cannot be confirmed as it stands, or null. Unresolved conflicts block by default -- the legacy rows disagree and a human must choose.

singletons_excluded.title: Singletons Excluded
singletons_excluded.description: One-off groups are not patterns and stay manual recipes (spec 6). They are counted, not listed.

writes_nothing.title: Writes Nothing
writes_nothing.description: Reading proposals never writes. Confirming does.

rank_delta.title: Rank Delta
rank_delta.description: Positive means margin-per-minute rates it HIGHER than margin % does.

RankedItemOut.title: RankedItemOut
RankedItemOut.description: One item's position in BOTH orderings. The disagreement is the finding (spec 5.6).

forecast.description: Null only when the caller asked for run_out=false. A WITHHELD forecast is a present Forecast with is_low_confidence=true and qty=null -- a different thing from not having asked.

daily_rate_qty.title: Daily Rate Qty
daily_rate_qty.description: Forecast daily consumption, or null when withheld.

days.title: Days
days.description: Days of cover left, as a decimal string.

on.title: On
on.description: Projected local date stock reaches zero.

RunOut.title: RunOut
RunOut.description:
Projected run-out, or the reason there is no date to show.

Invariant 9 governs this the same way it governs an order quantity: when the
forecast behind the date is low-confidence, `days` and `on` are null and
`forecast.reasons` is what the screen shows instead. A run-out date is the most
actionable number on the stock screen and therefore the worst one to guess at.

source.title: Source
source.description: 'supplier' (they told you) or 'packaging' (you read it off the pack).

ShelfLifeIn.title: ShelfLifeIn
ShelfLifeIn.description: A shelf life somebody checked. Never an estimate -- that is the default it leaves.

shelf_life_days.title: Shelf Life Days
shelf_life_days.description: Null means DOES NOT EXPIRE -- a statement, not a gap (ARCHITECTURE 8F.1).

usable_days.title: Usable Days
usable_days.description: Shelf life less transit buffer. The real cap on a cover window.

usable_days_after.title: Usable Days After
usable_days_after.description: What actually caps an order: shelf life less the transit buffer.

usable_days_changed_by.title: Usable Days Changed By
usable_days_changed_by.description: How far the ORDER CAP moved, which is the consequence worth reading. Null when there was no previous shelf life to compare against.

SkippedOut.title: SkippedOut
SkippedOut.description:
A candidate that produced no line, and which of the good reasons applied.

`is_capped` here is not a contradiction. A shelf-life cap can shorten the window far
enough that the forecast over it is already covered by stock on hand, so the cap
applied and *then* there was nothing to order. That is the cap working, and it is worth
saying: without it the reader sees an absent line and cannot tell "not needed" from
"the cap decided", which are different answers to "should I add this by hand?".

SourcingChoiceOut.title: SourcingChoiceOut
SourcingChoiceOut.description:
Which supplier won an ingredient and what choosing it cost. Spec 4.4.

`forgone_saving_pence` is the trade-off surfaced rather than resolved silently: a
cheaper option existed and was not taken, either because the saving was too small
to be worth a second invoice or because taking it would have pushed another
supplier's order below its minimum.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: Every qty on this response is theoretical. Counts are the source of truth.

batch_coverage_gap.title: Batch Coverage Gap
batch_coverage_gap.description: Theoretical on-hand less what the batches account for. A positive gap is stock FIFO and the expiry sweep cannot see, so it can never expire or be counted as waste.

unanchored.title: Unanchored
unanchored.description: No physical count behind the figure. Weak.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always DRAFT and nothing here can change it. Invariant 1: nothing is ordered without human confirmation, and confirmation happens in Telegram. This API has no endpoint that creates, confirms or sends a purchase order.

delivery_weekdays.title: Delivery Weekdays
delivery_weekdays.description: ISO 1..7. EMPTY means any day (walk-in retail).

terms_are_placeholders.title: Terms Are Placeholders
terms_are_placeholders.description: Six of eight suppliers' terms are INVENTED (ARCHITECTURE 8F.4). Every cover window built on them is only as good as the guess. This must reach the screen.

delivery_weekdays.title: Delivery Weekdays
delivery_weekdays.description: ISO 1..7. At least one: a supplier with no delivery day can never satisfy a cover window. A walk-in supplier delivers every day.

SupplierTermsIn.title: SupplierTermsIn
SupplierTermsIn.description:
Terms confirmed WITH the supplier. All of them together, on purpose.

`terms_are_placeholders` covers lead time, delivery days, cutoff, minimum,
fee and free-delivery threshold as one fact, because the cover window is
computed from several at once. Accepting a partial confirmation would clear
the warning on an order that is still partly fiction.

was_placeholder.title: Was Placeholder
was_placeholder.description: True if this call is what cleared the invented-terms warning.

changed.title: Changed
changed.description: Which terms actually moved, as 'label: before -> after'.

days_reported.title: Days Reported
days_reported.description: Days that reported at all. The rest are absent, not zero.

gross_pence.title: Gross Pence
gross_pence.description: Null when nothing reported at all. A window with no export is not a window in which the cafe took nothing.

caveats.title: Caveats
caveats.description: What could not be summed, and why. Print these; do not summarise.

source_note.title: Source Note
source_note.description: Where takings come from today. The Lightspeed payments endpoint has never been probed, so this is a back-office export.

TakingsResponse.title: TakingsResponse
TakingsResponse.description:
What the cafe took over a window, and how much of it is knowable.

Every nullable total means "some day in the window did not report it", never
zero. `net_pence` is null unless EVERY deduction was reported on EVERY day:
subtracting only the days that reported fees produces a net that is too high
and entirely plausible, which is the worst kind of wrong (invariant 8).

TemplateDetail.title: TemplateDetail
TemplateDetail.description: Everything the three-pane composition editor renders for one template.

TemplateItemOut.title: TemplateItemOut
TemplateItemOut.description: A sellable leaf of the template, with its cached cost and both margins.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: 'info' | 'watch' | 'act'. Colour is only for a crossed threshold.

UncostedItemOut.title: UncostedItemOut
UncostedItemOut.description:
A menu item with NO cached cost at all. Invariant 8, the strongest form.

These are not in `menu_item_cost` because their recipe does not resolve -- in the
seeded workbook, `'card' (£3.00)` and `Syrup Gift Set`, both on the known
data-quality list (ARCHITECTURE 8, 8.1). They are returned here rather than
silently absent: an item missing from the margin screen is indistinguishable from
an item nobody sells, and the honest answer is "we cannot say what this costs".
